blocks.html: This was a great conjecture, as we have represented above a, against the said du Tilh: inasmuch as of one who has been bad and wicked in the past there is great occasion to presume that he is still such, and perseveres in like malice b.

notes.citation: Coras, Annotation XXXVII (annot-037, p058), on the presumption that one once wicked remains so
notes.gloss: At p058 the printed and the counted numbers still agree.

notes.citation: Liber Sextus, De regulis iuris, regula 8 (Semel malus semper praesumitur esse malus)
notes.original: c. ſemel malus. de reg. iur.
notes.gloss: Once bad, always presumed bad — the maxim of the Sext, cited without in VI; the civil-law title D. 50.17 has no such rule.
